# Contact

How to reach neon1, when, and what the first call covers.

Tell me what's on your mind, or ask for an opinion on how your operations run today.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Email** | [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) |
| **Call or text** | [(424) 32-neon1](tel:+14243263661), that's (424) 326-3661 |
| **Book a call** | [calendly.com/1isgladtobeofservice/neon1-consultation](https://calendly.com/1isgladtobeofservice/neon1-consultation) |
| **LinkedIn** | [Pradeep](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pradeep-tathineni/) and [neon1](https://www.linkedin.com/company/neon1llc) |
| **GitHub** | [neon1llc](https://github.com/neon1llc) |

## What to expect

- **Where:** remote from anywhere, or on site within about 30 miles of Queens, NY.
- **When:** weekends 8am to 8pm and weekday evenings, Eastern time.
- **Size:** small jobs of a week or two up to projects of four to six weeks, with at most two clients at a time.
- **First call:** free and 15 minutes. The main pain points and your options.
- **After:** a short proposal with options and estimates. Nothing starts until you pick one.

## Availability and urgent issues

Work happens in planned appointments on weekday evenings and weekends. There's no 24/7 or emergency response. If something can't wait, such as a security incident in progress, an outage your business can't run without, or fraud on an account, contact a provider who offers emergency coverage, and your bank or the service involved, first. Ongoing care after a project, and any response times that come with it, are agreed in writing before they start.

Please leave passwords, health details, and payment information out of any first message.

docs.title: The names
docs.text:
# The names

Where neon1, its slogan and its products get their names.

## neon1

The name nods to Neo from *The Matrix*, who brought peace between man and machine. Neo means new. Neon is unmissable. It's always written with a lowercase n.

## "1 is glad to be of service."

The slogan nods to Robin Williams' Andrew from *Bicentennial Man*, a machine who spends two centuries being of service while searching for his humanity. The 1 is me, Pradeep, neon1's sole owner and your dedicated deputy, and 1 is glad to be of service.

## The legal names

- **neon1 LLC**, a New York limited liability company, does business as **neon1**, a registered assumed name (see the [state registration](registration.md)).
- **N1 Supply LLC** does business as **N1 Supply**. It is an affiliate of neon1 LLC.

## Product names

Repositories that neon1 builds mainly for its own use carry the `neon1-` prefix, such as neon1-site and neon1-corpus. Products made for the public or for clients get names of their own, such as [Ready, Secure, Go](../products/ready-secure-go.md).

docs.title: How a project runs
docs.text:
# How a project runs

Listen, propose, decide, build and hand over.

1. **Listen.** Show me how the work gets done today. One real example is enough.
2. **Propose.** A few options, from the quickest fix to the fuller build, each with an estimate, the effort, and what it gets you.
3. **Decide.** You pick. Sometimes that means a new system. Often it's a setting, a cleanup, or leaving it alone.
4. **Build.** Small changes, tested, and shown to you as they land.
5. **Hand over.** I show you how it works and write it down, so you can run it without me. Then I check it's doing what we agreed, and keep improving it if you want ongoing care.

Every project then runs through the same four layers in [1NEON](../products/1neon.md): Needs, Execute, Observe, Normalize. [See a sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example), start to finish, with made-up data, or [try the demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/).

docs.title: 1NEON help
docs.text:
# 1NEON help

Short answers about using the 1NEON client portal.

Short answers about using 1NEON. Signed in? Tap **?** at the top right of any page for help with that page.

## Getting started

### What is 1NEON?
The portal where you and I run your projects together. Each project keeps what you need, the work, the results, and the handover in one place. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### Can I try it first?
Yes, three ways, and none needs an account. The [guided walkthrough](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live) plays a fictional project on the real portal in about two minutes, with controls to pause, pick a chapter, or exit; the full story takes about six. The [interactive demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/) is a working copy with made-up clients where you pick who to be and try anything; your changes stay in your browser until you choose **Start over**. The [sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) is one made-up project to read at your own pace, from request to handover. With a couple of minutes to spare, start with the walkthrough. Short walkthroughs show a single thing: [joining from an invitation](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite), [adding a passkey](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey), [adding an authenticator app](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator), and [texts and text codes](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### How do I get in?
You need an invite. Open the link in your invite email and enter your email address. Sign in with a code sent to your email, or with a passkey. No password needed. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### I didn't get the sign-in code.
Check your spam or promotions folder, then wait a minute and choose **Send a new code**. Codes work for a few minutes, in the browser where you asked for them. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### Is there a tour?
Yes. It's offered the first time you sign in. Skip it or ask to be reminded next time, and replay it anytime from **?** at the top right or from your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

## Projects and the four layers

### What are Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize?
The four layers every project moves through, N E O N. **Needs** is what you want and the options to get there. **Execute** is the work. **Observe** checks the results against the goals. **Normalize** makes the change last: handover, training, and care. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### What should I do first on a project?
Look at **Next step** at the top of the project. It says what has to happen now and who it's waiting on, and it changes as soon as that's done: approve an option or send a file and it moves on to the next thing. When nothing is waiting on anyone, it names the stage's goal and offers **Move to** the next stage. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### What do Not assessed, On track, At risk, and Off track mean?
They're the project's health, which is someone's assessment of how it's going. A new project is **Not assessed**, and it stays that way when work starts or it moves to a new stage: starting work doesn't make a project on track. The team sets health on the project's overview, or with a status update, and the overview shows who set it and when. Items have their own status in their panel: To do, In progress, Blocked, or Done. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we rename, reorder, or hide stages?
Projects follow along. Their steps, the board, and Next step use the new names and order. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it. Decide keeps asking for an approved option, and Closed still ends a project, under any name or position.

### How do I tell you what I need?
Open the project's **Needs** tab and tap **Add request**. Finish a sentence with a few taps: what you'd like to do (choose any, or tap **+** to add your own), what it's for, what happens currently, how often it happens, and when it's due, including a date or a date range. Tap **Define another need** to add more. Each need becomes its own request, and only the first choice is required. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=needs).

### Do I have to write a lot?
No. Each section says what belongs there, shows an example, and offers suggestions you can add with one tap. Discovery questions take a short answer right where they're asked, and a real example helps most. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### How do I know when something changes?
The bell at the top glows softly when something new happens, like a file upload, a decision, or a project moving stage. Tap it to see what changed and who did it, then tap one to open it. Important changes also email you; choose which in your profile under **Notifications**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### How do I comment or change an item?
Tap the item's title. A panel opens with its status, owner, due date, and details, and a place to comment. Everyone in your organization sees the comments. Options and measures open the same way, with their cost and scores, or unit and target, there too. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### How do I check something off?
Tick the box beside it. Every item that can be finished has one, and the counts on each tab and section show how many are done. A choice between options counts as one, done once an option is approved, and a measure counts as done when it reaches its target. Status updates and decisions are records, so they don't count. Files you upload aren't counted either; a **File needed** is, and it's checked off when you send the file. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

### How do I delete something?
Use the trash button on the item, or **Delete** in its panel. Either one asks first. Approved options and decisions can't be deleted, since they're the record of what was agreed; options themselves come from neon1. Files have their own **Delete** for the person who uploaded them and admins.

### What does the onion next to a project mean?
It shows progress. Needs is the center ring and Normalize is the outside one; each ring fills as that layer's work gets done.

### What does the board show?
Every project as a card, in the stage it's in. Columns run left to right from the first call to care after handover. Drag a card to move it, or use its **Move to** menu on a phone. A closed project moves back the same way, or use **Reopen** on its page. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What does the timeline show?
Under **Projects**, **Timeline** draws each project from the day it started to its target date, colored by its layer. The dashed line is today, the diamond is the target, the lighter part is time still ahead, and red stripes are time past the target. Each row also says its stage and how many days are left. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=care).

### How do I start a project?
Choose **New project**, answer a few short questions, and the project starts with a checklist that fits. You can change everything later. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### What is the calendar on Home?
A whole month at a time, named at the top. The arrows step a month back or forward, **Today** comes back, and the month list jumps anywhere from a year back to two years ahead. Each mark is something dated: a task's due date, a milestone, a project's target, or one of your organization's own events. Choose a day to see what's on it. Editors can add leave or time off, an office closure or event, a meeting, or a care plan date (a monthly call, a retro, a re-check), for one day or several, at a time or all day, and set it to repeat every week or month. Below the month, **Past** and **Repeated** start folded, and **Overdue** and **Upcoming** start open. Leave in the next seven days also shows under **Away this week**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=calendar).

### What is Insights?
Charts made from your organization's own data: open and overdue work, how often things finish on time, days to a decision, work finished per week, where projects sit across the four layers, and how healthy they are. Work counts as finished on the day it was marked done, so editing it later doesn't move it; if it's reopened and finished again, the latest finish counts. The page explains how each number is counted. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=observe).

## Proposals, decisions, and signing

### What is a proposal revision?
neon1's options for a project are issued together as a numbered proposal, such as 0039-r1, and each option in it gets its own ID, such as 0039-r1-B. Issuing a revision freezes a copy of everything it shows, so what you approve is exactly what you read. If the options change, neon1 issues the next revision (0039-r2); earlier ones stay readable, marked as replaced. Each revision also shows when its prices were checked; after the recheck date, approval waits until neon1 refreshes it. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### How do I approve an option?
Open the project's **Needs** layer, compare the options, and choose **Approve this option**. You can add conditions, such as "only after 6pm". Then type your full name and tick the box to sign; your typed name is your signature. The approval is recorded with your signature, your name, the time, and a copy of the option's terms (title, description, price, hours, timeline, and outside costs) exactly as you saw them. Options come from neon1; to ask for a change, comment on the option. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I download the proposal?
Yes. Under the options, choose **Read the full proposal**. It puts the discovery, the goals, every option with what's in and out, the hours and prices, what each of us will do, and the agreement on one page. Use **Print or save as PDF** to keep a copy or sign it on paper. Signing your approval in 1NEON counts the same as signing it on paper. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Who can approve?
The person named as the project's decision maker. If nobody is named, an admin of your organization can. Only an admin of your organization can name or change the decision maker, under **People** on the project's overview, after confirming it's them; editors can change everyone else on the project. Each change is recorded with the old and new decision maker, and neon1 can't be named, since it proposes the options. (In neon1's own organization, where neon1 is the client, it can.) [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can an approval be changed?
Not edited. Once approved, neither the decision nor the option it came from can be edited or removed. To change course, a new option is proposed and approved; the earlier decision stays on record, marked as replaced, so the history stays clear.

### What does approving an option commit us to?
An approval records that your organization agreed to that option as shown: its scope, cost, and timeline, plus any conditions you added. Both sides can rely on that record. It works alongside your signed agreement with neon1, which governs the paid work.

### How do I accept a handover step?
On the project's **Normalize** layer, steps that need your sign-off show **Check it and accept**. Note what you checked if you like, type your full name, and tick the box to sign. The acceptance is recorded with your signature and can't be edited afterwards. When the last step is accepted, neon1 prepares the final invoice. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

### What do Cost, Quality, and Effort mean?
They're neon1's assessment of each option, from 1 to 5, where more filled dots is always better. **Cost** is the total cost. **Quality** is how fully it meets the requirements you agreed. **Effort** is your team's effort to adopt and run it. Each option also lists one-time and recurring charges apart, with a first-year total when it has both; the written price on the option is what you'd agree to. Figures in the demo and the walkthrough are illustrative. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

## Files

### How do I send a file?
Use **Upload** next to a file I asked for, or go to **Files** and upload it there. Pick the project it belongs to. Tap a file's name to open it: PDFs, pictures, and text open in a new tab, and anything else downloads. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### Are files safe?
Every file is checked for viruses before anyone can download it, and stays private to your organization. Please don't upload passwords or keys.

### What can I upload?
Any kind of file, up to 100 MB each. Please don't upload passwords, keys, or other secrets, malware, or regulated data such as health or payment card details unless we have a written agreement that covers it.

## People and access

### What can viewers, editors, and admins do?
Viewers read and comment. Editors also add and change work. Admins also invite people, change their access, and change settings. neon1's own access is set by neon1, so it shows on People without a way to change it. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### How do I invite someone?
Admins go to **People** and choose **Invite people**. The person gets an email with a link. People shows whether each invitation email went out; if one didn't, or it got lost, choose **Resend**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### Can 1NEON text me?
Once texts are switched on, yes. Add your mobile number on your profile, agree to texts, save, then type the code 1NEON texts you. Texts only say that something new is waiting, with a link; they never name your organization, projects, or files. Reply STOP to any text to turn them off. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### Why does it ask me to confirm it's me?
Admin actions (inviting people, changing access or settings, and deleting a project or someone else's comment or file) also need a recent confirmation with a passkey, an authenticator app, or a text-message code. That way a stolen email account isn't enough to make changes. On your profile, under Two-step verification, add any of the three, then confirm with it when asked. A second one is a backup if you lose the first. Once confirmed, you won't be asked again for 12 hours in that sign-in. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

### Can I use an authenticator app?
Yes. On your profile, choose **Set up** next to Authenticator app, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type the 6-digit code it shows. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator).

### What's a passkey?
A sign-in that uses your face, fingerprint, or device PIN instead of a code. It's faster, and it's phishing-resistant: it only works on the real 1NEON site, so a look-alike page can't use it. Add one on your profile under Two-step verification; next time you sign in, 1NEON offers it first. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

## Your account

### How do I change my name or the look?
Open your profile from the menu. You can change your name, title, theme, menu, and notifications there, then choose **Save**. The menu button (top left, and Menu at the bottom on phones) opens the full menu; choose **Mini** to also keep a slim menu of icons on the left. Two-step verification and signing out work right away. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=profile).

### How do I sign out?
Open your profile and choose **Sign out**.

### I lost my phone or my authenticator app.
You can still sign in with a code sent to your email. The second step is only needed for admin actions, such as inviting people or changing settings. If you set up another method, confirm it's you with that one, then remove the lost one under Two-step verification on your profile and add a new one. If you've lost every method, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) from your account's address. Email alone isn't enough to remove a second step, since a stolen mailbox is exactly what it guards against, so I confirm who you are another way first: a call to a phone number already on record for you or your organization (never one given in the email), and, if your organization has another admin, their written OK as well. Then I remove the lost methods, note what was done and when, and email you that it's done; you add a new one on your profile. Until then, email codes still sign you in, and only admin actions wait. The portal has no self-service reset for a lost second step.

### My email address changed.
Your email address is how 1NEON knows you, and it can't be changed on your profile. Ask an admin of your organization to invite your new address and deactivate the old one, or email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech). Work done under the old address stays in the record under that name.

### Who do I ask for access?
An admin of your organization. Admins invite people and change their access. If you don't know who that is, or neon1's own access needs to change, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

## Invoices and paying

### Where are invoices and payments?
Under the project's **Execute** layer, in **Invoices**, with what's paid and what's left on each. When one is ready or overdue, **Next step** at the top of the project says so and links to it. Each invoice opens on neon1's letterhead with its number, lines, due date, and how to pay, ready to print or save as a PDF. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### How do I pay an invoice?
Choose **Pay** on the invoice. Stripe's secure page opens, where you pay by bank transfer (ACH, preferred) or card; 1NEON never sees your bank or card details. A card payment shows as paid within a minute, and a bank transfer once it clears, usually in a few business days. You can also pay by check, Zelle, or wire, with the invoice number in the memo, and neon1 records it when it arrives. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### When are invoices sent?
As the option you approved says. For a fixed price, half is invoiced when you approve, as a deposit, and the rest when you accept the handover. Items neon1 buys for you are billed at cost with the receipt, and a care plan is billed monthly. Invoices are due in 15 days unless the option says otherwise, and each one emails whoever is set to get billing notices. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### Can an invoice be changed?
Not once it's issued. An issued invoice is numbered and kept exactly as issued. A mistake is fixed with a credit that reduces it, or by voiding it with a reason, and both stay on record. An invoice that has a payment can't be voided.

### What is the service agreement?
neon1's terms for all work with your organization: how work is agreed, paying, ownership, confidentiality, and how either of us can end it. An admin of your organization signs it once in 1NEON (open it from **Settings**), before the first option can be approved, and it covers every project. You can read it any time at [/1NEON/agreement](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/agreement). [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

## Support and your data

### Something urgent is wrong. Who do I tell?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) with what happened and when. neon1 is one person working planned hours, with no 24/7 or emergency response, so for something that can't wait, such as a fraud on your bank account or an outage your business can't run without, contact the provider responsible first. Report a security problem in the portal itself to [security@neon1.tech](mailto:security@neon1.tech).

### Can we get a copy of our data?
Yes. There's no export button, so ask at [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) and I'll send your organization's data in a common format.

### What happens to our data when the work ends?
It's kept as the record of our work together, so either of us can refer back to it, unless your organization asks me to delete it. Your organization can stop using 1NEON at any time and ask for an export first. The [privacy policy](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/privacy) has the details, including how long backups and audit records last.

### Who can I contact?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

docs.text:
# Working with neon1

Short answers on where, when, how long, how much, and how data is handled.

## Do you come on site?

Yes, within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. I also work remotely, or on your own network through a secure connection that I set up for the job and that's removed when it's done.

## When do you work?

Saturdays and Sundays from 8am to 8pm, and weekday evenings from 6pm (until 9pm Monday to Thursday, 8pm on Friday), Eastern time, typically with 10 to 20 hours a week for project work. The booking calendar shows what's open.

## What if something urgent comes up?

I work in planned appointments on weekday evenings and weekends, and I don't offer 24/7 or emergency response. Urgent issues, such as a security incident in progress or an outage you can't run without, need a provider with emergency coverage. Ongoing care after a project is agreed in writing, including any response times. Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) for anything else.

## How long does a project take?

Small jobs take a week or two, medium ones two to four weeks, and bigger projects four to six. I take on up to two clients at a time so each one gets proper attention.

## How is the cost worked out?

After the first call I send a short proposal with options, usually a quick fix, a solid setup, and a fuller build. Each comes with a cost estimate and says what it covers and how much effort it takes, how much is automated, what upkeep it needs, and how well it copes when something fails. Every option meets the same baseline for security and quality; a smaller option does less, not worse. You pick one. If the scope or the work changes along the way, I'll tell you before it changes the cost. [See how options look in 1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

## How do you treat our data and accounts?

Before any paid work, we sign a short [service agreement](../policies/service-agreement.md) once, in 1NEON or on paper. It covers how I'll handle your systems and information: only the access the job needs, kept confidential, and handed back or removed when we're done. After that, each project is a [proposal](../examples/proposal-options.md) with options, and choosing one, signed on paper or in 1NEON, is what we both agree to. It works both ways, so you'll know what I need from you and why. If the work touches personal or health data, the right agreement, such as a Business Associate Agreement, comes first. [See a handover in 1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

## How do I pay?

Invoices come through [1NEON](../products/1neon.md), in the project they belong to, and are due within 15 days. A fixed-price project usually starts with a deposit of half the price, and the rest is billed once you accept the handover. You can pay online by bank transfer (ACH) or card through Stripe, or by check, Zelle, or wire. There's no surcharge for any of them. If I buy equipment or software for you, you pay back exactly what the receipt shows, with no markup.

## Do you run security training?

Yes, for groups from parents and teachers to engineers and executives. Sessions cover the threats people meet most, such as phishing, fraud, and data brokers, plus accounts and passwords, home and business networks, cameras and smart devices, and physical security. For organizations I also cover privacy policies, data handling, security frameworks, and incident response.

## What don't you do?

I don't repair electronics, though I can debug software and hardware installs and get them working together. I don't handle personal or health data without the right agreements in place, such as a Business Associate Agreement, but I can help you get them. I'm not a lawyer, but I'll work alongside yours on the technical side.

# 1NEON

The neon1 client portal that comes with a client engagement, where each project runs from the first call to handover.

The neon1 client portal at [neon1.tech/1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/). Each project runs through four layers: Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize. Proposals, signed decisions, files, invoices, and results stay together from the first call to handover.

- **Available now,** as part of working with neon1. It comes with a client engagement and isn't sold on its own.
- **Who it helps:** the people at a client organization who follow a project, send files, and approve options, and the administrators who decide who can see what.
- **For example,** I issue a proposal with two options for a project, numbered 0039-r1. The person named as decision maker compares them and signs their approval of 0039-r1-B with a typed name, and 1NEON keeps their signature, the time, and a copy of the option's terms as they saw them. The deposit invoice follows in the same project, and they can pay it by bank transfer or card.

## Current limits

- Access is by invitation only, from neon1 or an administrator of your organization.
- Online payments go through Stripe Checkout, by bank transfer (ACH) or card. Checks, Zelle, and wires are recorded by hand when they arrive.
- There's no export button. A copy of your organization's data is sent on request.
- Text messages work only once they're switched on and you've agreed to them on your profile.

## Next step

[See a sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) or [try the demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/), which runs in your browser with made-up data. To use 1NEON for real, start with [a first call](../company/contact.md). For help inside the portal, see [1NEON help](../faq/1neon-help.md).

Code: [neon1llc/neon1-1NEON](https://github.com/neon1llc/neon1-1NEON).

# Service agreement

neon1's service agreement, as a client organization signs it once in 1NEON: how work is agreed, purchases, paying, ownership, confidentiality, records, quality, limits, and ending.

**The short version**

- One agreement covers every project. Each project's scope, price, and timeline come from the option your decision maker approves and signs.
- Invoices are due in 15 days. Anything I buy for you is paid back at cost.
- An admin signs it once in 1NEON with a typed name. Either of us can end it with 14 days' notice.

Edition 1.0

This agreement is between neon1 LLC, doing business as neon1 ("neon1", "I", "me"), and the organization named where it is signed in 1NEON ("you"). It covers every project I do for you while it is in effect.

## How work is agreed

Each project has a proposal in 1NEON, issued in numbered revisions. When your decision maker approves an option, its ID (for example 0039-r2-B) fixes that project's scope, price, and timeline. A change is agreed the same way, by approving an option in the next revision. This agreement governs everything else, and if a proposal and this agreement disagree, this agreement wins.

## Purchases

Prices for equipment, software, and services from other vendors are estimates. You buy them yourself, unless an approval says that I buy them for you. When I do, you pay me back exactly what I paid, shown by the receipt in 1NEON, with no markup.

## Paying

I send invoices through 1NEON. Each one is due within 15 days unless it says otherwise. A fixed-price option may ask for a deposit when it is approved, as the proposal states. You can pay by bank transfer (ACH), card, check, Zelle, or wire. If an invoice is more than 30 days overdue, I may pause work until it is paid, after telling you.

## What you provide

You give me timely answers, the access the work needs, and accounts held in your organization's name. Please don't put passwords or other secrets in 1NEON.

## Ownership

Once you have paid for a project, what I made for you in it is yours. I keep my general know-how and the tools I had before or build for my own use, and open-source software stays under its own license.

## Confidentiality

We each keep what we learn about the other's business private, and use it only for the work. This doesn't cover what is already public or what the law requires us to disclose.

## Regulated data

I don't handle health records, payment card data, or similar regulated personal data unless we sign a separate agreement for it first, such as a business associate agreement.

## Records

I keep project records, signed approvals, invoices, and receipts, and I don't delete them on a schedule. If you ask me to delete something, I will, except what the law requires me to keep.

## Quality

I do the work with care. If something I delivered doesn't work as agreed and you tell me within 30 days of handover, I fix it at no charge.

## Limits

My total liability for any claim is limited to what you paid me for that project in the 12 months before the claim. Neither of us is liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses, such as lost profits.

## Ending

Either of us may end this agreement with 14 days' written notice, by message in 1NEON or by email. You pay for the work done and the purchases made up to that point.

## Signing and law

We agree to sign and keep these records electronically, and a name typed in 1NEON is a signature. You can ask me for a paper copy at any time. New York law governs this agreement.

# 1NEON guide: overview, names, and addresses

What 1NEON is, how its frame works, every kind of ID and name it shows, and the address of every page.

1NEON is neon1's client portal at neon1.tech/1NEON. Each client organization runs its projects there with neon1. Every project moves through four layers, N E O N: **Needs** (what's wanted, and the options to get there), **Execute** (the work), **Observe** (the results checked against the goals), and **Normalize** (handover, training, and care, so the change lasts). This guide describes every page, state, and action, so Neo can explain any of them, link to them, show them in a tour, and plan any action with a signed-in person.

## Who's who

- **neon1** is Pradeep's one-person business. In 1NEON, neon1 is the *operator*: it proposes options, does the work, and can enter every client organization. The operator role comes from sign-in configuration, never from data in the portal.
- **A client organization** (also called an organization, a client, or a tenant) is one business or household neon1 works with. Its people are invited by its admins or by neon1.
- **neon1's own organization** has the slug `neon1` and the client ID **N1-0001**. There neon1 is also the client, so neon1's people may approve options and name decision makers, which they can't do in any other organization.
- **A member** is a person in an organization, with one access level there: viewer, editor, or admin. One person can belong to several organizations with a different level in each.

## IDs and names people see

| Looks like | What it is | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `N1-0001`, `N1-0002` | An organization's **client ID**, numbered in the order clients joined. N1-0001 is neon1 itself. Used in the organization chooser, on All clients, and on invoices. | Chooser, All clients, organization header |
| `acme-dental` | An organization's **slug**, its handle in addresses | `/1NEON/o/acme-dental/...` |
| `FLOW-1`, `MIG-2`, `HOME-1`, `PRJ-3` | A **project key**: a prefix from the project's template plus a number counted per organization and prefix | Cards, lists, the project page, search |
| `0039`, `0039-r2` | A **proposal number** and one of its **revisions**. Each project has one proposal; the first 1NEON issued is 0039, and each change is issued as the next revision | The proposal strip under Options, the proposal page, its PDF and Word copies |
| `0039-r2-B` | An **option ID**: the revision and the option's letter. A decision names the ID it approved | Options, decisions, purchases bought for an option |
| `INV-0039-01` | An **invoice number**: the proposal's number (or the project key when there's no proposal) and the invoice's place in the project. Set when neon1 issues it | Invoices, the invoice page, card statements (`NEON1* INV003901`) |
| Item titles | Items (requests, tasks, options, measures, and so on) are shown by title; their IDs only appear in links (`#item-…`) | Inside a project |

Project key prefixes come from the template chosen in New project: Blank is `PRJ`, Cloud migration is `MIG`, Workflow automation is `FLOW`, AI assistant is `AI`, Security readiness is `SEC`, and Personal or home tech is `HOME`. The number after the dash counts up per prefix within one organization, so `MIG-1` in two organizations are two different projects.

## The frame around every signed-in page

- **Menu** (top left; **Menu** at the bottom on phones) opens every page: Home, Board, Projects, Files, Insights, People, Settings, the four layers, and your profile. Choosing **Mini** on the profile also keeps a slim column of icons on the left.
- **Organization chooser** at the top of the menu switches between organizations a person belongs to. neon1 also sees **All clients** there.
- **Search** (the search button, Ctrl K or ⌘K, or `/`) jumps to any page or project and starts common actions: Start a new project and Upload a file for editors and admins, Invite people for admins.
- **?** (top right) opens help for the page in view: what it's for, a few how-tos, **Show me on this page** (a spotlight tour of that page), and **Full tour**.
- **The bell** glows when something new happened in the organization: a file upload, a decision, a stage move, a new comment, and similar. Opening it lists what changed and who did it.
- **Neo** sits at the bottom right: the assistant that answers questions, links to pages, runs tours, and, with the person's go-ahead, does things for them.
- **A read-only banner** shows on All clients: "read only. Open a client to make changes."

## Themes

A person picks a look on their profile: **Awake** (light, the default), **Matrix** (dark, green on black, like the landing page's rain), or **Device** (follows the device's light or dark setting). Neo's window follows the same look as the page around it.

## Addresses

Every signed-in page lives under `https://neon1.tech/1NEON/`. In the table, `{org}` is the organization's slug and `{KEY}` a project key.

| Page | Address |
|---|---|
| Sign-in | `/1NEON/` |
| Home (the organization's starting page) | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace` |
| Board | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow` |
| Projects (list and timeline) | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects` |
| New project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new` |
| One project, Overview | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}` |
| One project, a layer | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, or `/normalize` |
| Options on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs#options` |
| The project's proposal | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal` |
| A project's invoices | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/execute#billing` |
| One invoice | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{invoiceId}` |
| The service agreement, to sign | `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` |
| Files asked for on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs#files` |
| One item on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/{layer}#item-{itemId}` |
| One layer across all projects | `/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/needs` (also `execute`, `observe`, `normalize`) |
| People | `/1NEON/o/{org}/people` |
| Files | `/1NEON/o/{org}/documents` |
| Insights | `/1NEON/o/{org}/insights` |
| Settings | `/1NEON/o/{org}/settings` |
| Your profile | `/1NEON/me` (two-step verification at `/1NEON/me#security`) |
| All clients (neon1 only) | `/1NEON/all/workflow` |
| FAQs, public | `/1NEON/faqs` |
| Sample project, public | `/1NEON/example` |
| Guided walkthrough, public | `/1NEON/live` (short ones: `?play=invite`, `passkey`, `authenticator`, `texts`, `start`, `needs`, `listen`, `propose`, `decide`, `build`, `observe`, `handover`, `care`, `team`, `profile`, `signin`) |
| Interactive demo, public | `/1NEON/demo/` |
| Privacy, terms, cookies, service agreement | `/1NEON/privacy`, `/1NEON/terms`, `/1NEON/cookies`, `/1NEON/agreement` |

The address word for Execute is `execute` and for Normalize is `normalize`. Older links that say `execution` or `next` still work.

## Spotlight anchors

Tours point at named spots on a page. Each name below exists only on the page listed, and only while that part is on screen.

| Anchor | Page | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `nav-home`, `nav-board`, `nav-projects`, `nav-layers`, `nav-files`, `nav-me` | Every page | Menu entries (the menu must be open, or Mini on) |
| `menu` | Every page | The menu button |
| `search` | Every page | The search button |
| `help` | Every page | The ? button |
| `notifications` | Organization pages | The bell |
| `needs-you`, `coming-up`, `get-started`, `activity` | Home | Needs you, Coming up, Get started, Recent activity |
| `board-column`, `board-card` | Board, All clients | A stage column, a project card |
| `new-project`, `project-list` | Projects | New project button, the list |
| `next-step`, `stage`, `layers` | One project | Next step box, the stage line, the layer tabs |
| `proposal` | One project, Needs | The proposal strip under Options: the revision, its price check, and Issue or Read the proposal |
| `wizard` | New project | The questions |
| `layer-list` | One layer across projects | The list |
| `invite`, `people-list` | People | Invite people, the list of people |
| `upload` | Files | The upload area |
| `kpis`, `weekly`, `by-layer` | Insights | The numbers on top, Finished per week, Projects by layer |
| `stages` | Settings | The stage rows |
| `passkey` | Profile | Two-step verification |

docs.title: 1NEON guide: projects, stages, layers, and items
docs.text:
# 1NEON guide: projects, stages, layers, and items

How a project moves through stages and the four layers, every kind of item and its states, Next step, health, the proposal and its revisions, signed approvals, purchases, handover acceptance, invoices, and payments.

## A project

A project is one piece of work for one organization. It has a key (such as `FLOW-1`), a name, a one or two sentence summary, an outcome ("what will be true when it's done"), a target date, a stage, a health, the people on it with their roles, sensitive-data flags (PII, PHI, or payment data), and items in four layers. Every change is recorded with who made it and when, and every edit carries the version the person last saw, so two people can't silently overwrite each other: the later save is told what changed and asked to choose.

A project can be **archived** (kept, read only, off the main lists; **Restore from archive** brings it back) or moved to **Trash** by an admin, who types the project's key to confirm. A trashed project disappears from every view but is kept, and it's erased only if the client asks.

## Stages and the board

An organization's workflow is a row of stages, each tied to one layer. The default stages, in order:

| Stage | Layer | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | Needs | Fit call held |
| Listen | Needs | Discovery complete, baseline metrics recorded |
| Propose | Needs | Options published to the client |
| Decide | Needs | An option approved |
| Build | Execute | All milestone tasks done (limit: 3 projects at once) |
| Verify | Observe | Checks pass, after metrics recorded |
| Hand over | Normalize | Handoff checklist signed off |
| Care | Normalize | Ongoing care, or closed |
| Closed | Normalize | (the end) |

The **Board** shows every project as a card in its stage's column, with the column's "Done when" line and how many projects it holds. A card shows the key, name, health, and how long it has been in the stage. Editors and admins drag a card to another column, or use its **Move to** menu on a phone. Admins can rename stages, change "Done when", set a limit, reorder, and hide stages in **Settings** (saving asks them to confirm it's them). A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it.

Two stages keep their roles under any name or position: **Decide** is the gate (moving forward past it without an approved option is allowed but asks for a reason, which is recorded), and **Closed** ends a project. A closed project is finished. **Reopen** on its page, or dragging it back, moves it to the stage before. Moving backward never asks for a reason. Moving a stage never changes health.

**All clients** (neon1 only) is the same board across every organization, read only, grouped by organization or as one board.

## The four layers and their items

A project page has tabs: **Overview**, **Needs**, **Execute**, **Observe**, and **Normalize**. Each layer tab groups its items by kind. The onion beside the project's name has one ring per layer, Needs in the center, and each ring fills as that layer's work gets done.

| Kind | Layer | What it is | Statuses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request | Needs | Something the client wants, built as a sentence of taps: what, what for, what happens today, how often, and when | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Discovery question | Needs | A question for the people who do the work, answered in their words | same |
| System or account (asset) | Needs | A system, account, vendor, or data source the work touches. Never passwords | same |
| Requirement | Needs | Something the result must do, with a priority: must, should, or could | same |
| Option | Needs | One way to solve it, from neon1: cost, timeline, and scores for cost, quality, and effort (1 to 5, more is better), and whether neon1 recommends it | Draft, Proposed (shared for approval), Declined, Approved |
| Decision | Needs | The permanent record of an approved option, with the approver's signature | Approved (a record, can't change) |
| Constraint or assumption | Needs | Something the work depends on or is limited by, printed in the proposal | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Proposal revision | Needs | One issued, frozen revision of the project's proposal, such as 0039-r1. Made only by **Issue the proposal** | a record |
| File needed | Needs | A file neon1 asked the client for | Done once the file is sent |
| Task | Execute | One piece of work someone can finish | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Milestone | Execute | A point everyone can see, such as a launch | same |
| Change request | Execute | A change to what was agreed, with its effect on cost and dates | same |
| Purchase | Execute | Something to buy for the approved option: estimate, actual cost, where it was bought, who buys it (the client or neon1), and its receipt | Open, Bought, Installed (done), Returned |
| Invoice | Execute | A bill for the work or for purchases, numbered when issued (such as INV-0039-01) | Draft, Issued, Paid, Void. Partly paid and overdue are worked out from payments and the due date |
| Payment | Execute | Money received against one invoice, from Stripe or recorded by neon1 | a record |
| Status update | Execute | One line on how it's going, with a health; posting it sets the project's health | a record |
| Measure (metric) | Observe | A number that shows it worked: unit, baseline, target, which way is better, and dated readings | Done when it reaches its target |
| Check | Observe | Something to test before calling it done | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Incident | Observe | Something that broke: what people saw, when, and what fixed it | same |
| Handoff | Normalize | A step before it's fully the client's, such as admin access transferred | same |
| Runbook | Normalize | Written steps for a job that comes up again | same |
| Training | Normalize | Who learns what, and how | same |
| Care | Normalize | Ongoing care after launch | same |
| Retro | Normalize | What went well, or what to do differently | same |

Any item opens in a panel by tapping its title: status, owner (assignee), due date, details, and comments. The box beside an item ticks it done. Tab and section counts show done out of total. A choice between options counts as one, done once an option is approved. Status updates, decisions, proposal revisions, invoices, payments, and uploaded files aren't counted.

Who may do what with items:

- Anyone who can read the project (viewers too) may add a **request** and comment.
- Editors and admins add, edit, tick off, and delete other items.
- **Options** come only from neon1: neon1 writes, shares (Proposed), and withdraws them. A client who wants a different option comments on it or adds a request.
- **Proposal revisions**, **invoices**, and **payments** come only from neon1, through their own buttons, and an issued one can't be edited or deleted.
- An **approved option** and its **decision** can't be edited or deleted. To change course, neon1 proposes a new option and it's approved on its own. The earlier decision stays on record, marked as replaced.

## Options and the proposal

Options are compared on the Needs tab under Options (`#options`). Each shows its cost (one-time and recurring charges apart, with a first-year total when there are both), timeline, the three scores, and a Recommended mark. Each option can also carry neon1's estimated hours, the costs paid directly to vendors, the purchases it expects (what, why, an example, an estimated price, and whether the client or neon1 buys it), and the result the client can check.

A project has one proposal, issued in numbered revisions. While neon1 is still shaping the options, the proposal is a **draft**: the client can read it and the options, but can't approve yet. When the options are ready, neon1 chooses **Issue the proposal**, which freezes a copy of everything the proposal shows and numbers it. The first proposal 1NEON issued is 0039, and its first revision is **0039-r1**. Every option in a revision gets an ID made of the revision and a letter, such as **0039-r1-B**, and the decision names that ID.

A later change (an edited option, a new one, a refreshed estimate, or a change of scope) is issued as the next revision, 0039-r2. Earlier revisions stay readable, marked "Replaced by a later revision", and no revision can be edited or deleted.

**Read the proposal**, under the options, opens `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal`: discovery, goals, constraints and assumptions, every shared option with what's in and out, a cost table, what each side will do, and the agreement, in neon1's letterhead look. It shows the latest revision, with earlier ones a choice away. **Print or save as PDF** prints only the proposal, with its ID and page number on every page. **Download Word** saves the revision as a Word file named like `neon1-{org}-proposal-0039-r1.docx`. The ID is in the file name, the document's properties, and the header on every page, so when a marked-up copy is uploaded to Files, 1NEON asks "Is this a revision of Proposal 0039-r1?" and files it under Files, Proposals, with the revision it answers.

### Price checks

Estimates are checked when a revision is issued and rechecked after 30 days. Past that date, approval waits: the decision maker chooses **Ask neon1 to refresh**, and neon1 issues the next revision with checked prices. A revision doesn't expire in any other way.

### Changes of scope

A request added after an option is approved asks "Does this change what was approved?" with **Yes, it changes it**, **No**, or **Not sure**. A request marked as a change is flagged for the next revision, and neon1 answers it there.

## Approving and signing

**Approve this option** is offered only to the person allowed to approve on that project:

- the project's named **decision maker**, or several, any of whom may approve;
- if nobody is named, an **admin of the client organization**;
- never neon1, which proposed the options, except in neon1's own organization (N1-0001), where neon1 is the client.

Neo never approves for anyone. Asked to, it points to **Approve this option**.

Approving is possible only when all of these hold, and 1NEON says which one is missing:

1. neon1 has issued the proposal, and the option is in the latest revision.
2. The option hasn't changed since that revision was issued. Otherwise it waits for the next one.
3. The revision is within its price check.
4. An admin of the client organization has signed neon1's [service agreement](../policies/service-agreement.md) at its current edition. (Not needed in N1-0001.)

Approving restates exactly what's being accepted: the option and its ID, the proposal it's from, the estimate, the timeline, neon1's hours, what's paid directly to vendors, what's to buy, and the result to check. The approver may add conditions ("only after 6pm"). Then they type their full name and tick the consent box: "I agree to sign electronically. My typed name is my signature, and I can ask neon1 for a paper copy at any time."

The decision records the option ID, the approver's name and email, the time, the option's version, a copy of its terms exactly as shown, and the signature: the typed name, the consent, a SHA-256 fingerprint of the terms that were signed, and the address and browser it came from. If the option changed after the person opened it, the approval is refused and they review it again. A signed approval records that the organization agreed to that option's scope, cost, and timeline, and it counts the same as signing the proposal on paper. The printed proposal and its Word copy show the signature.

Approving also does two things on its own:

- The option's expected purchases join Execute, marked with its ID.
- If the option's price is fixed, neon1 gets a draft deposit invoice to check and issue. Nothing is sent to the client until neon1 issues it.

Only an admin of the client, after confirming it's them, can name or change a project's decision maker, under People on the project's Overview. Editors can change everyone else on the project. neon1 can't be named decision maker, except in its own organization.

## The service agreement

neon1's service agreement covers every project with an organization: how work is agreed, purchases, paying, what the client provides, ownership, confidentiality, regulated data, records, quality, limits, ending, and signing. Anyone can read it at `/1NEON/agreement`. An admin of the client organization signs it once on `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement`, reached from **Settings** or from the notice under the options ("Before approving, sign neon1's service agreement"), with a typed name and the consent box, before the first option can be approved. The signature records the edition (now 1.0), a SHA-256 fingerprint of its exact text, the time, and where it came from. A new edition is signed again before the next approval, and an earlier signature always keeps the text it was given. The agreement's full text is in the [service agreement](../policies/service-agreement.md).

## Purchases

Purchases sit in Execute under **Purchases**, filled in from the approved option's expected purchases. Each shows its estimate, what was actually paid and where, who buys it, and its receipt. A bought item without a receipt is flagged. Statuses are **Open**, **Bought**, **Installed** (done), and **Returned**.

- **The client buys it** ("You buy it."): in the organization's name, keeping the receipt with the project (**Attach the receipt**).
- **neon1 buys it**: only after the decision maker agrees, with their initials, that neon1 buys it and is paid back at cost. The initials come from the signed approval, or the decision maker adds them later on the purchase. Until then the purchase says "Waiting on the decision maker's initials before neon1 buys it." neon1 attaches the receipt, and the cost is billed on a reimbursement invoice at exactly what the receipt shows, with no markup.

## Handover acceptance

Handoff steps in Normalize can be checked and accepted by the decision maker with **Check it and accept**: an optional note on what they checked ("What you checked"), then **Sign and accept** with a typed name and the consent box, the same way as an approval. The step is marked done with the signature, and the acceptance shows on the project's handover. When the last handoff step is accepted, neon1 gets a draft final invoice for what's left on the approved price.

## Invoices and paying

Invoices are under the project's **Execute** layer, in **Invoices** (`#billing`). neon1 makes them; the client sees them once they're issued, never as drafts.

| Type | When it comes up |
|---|---|
| Deposit | Drafted when a fixed-price option is approved: half the price by default |
| Progress | Added by neon1 for a stage of the work |
| Final | Drafted when the last handover step is accepted: what's left on the approved price |
| Purchases at cost | Reimbursement for what neon1 bought, from the receipts |
| Care plan | The monthly fee for ongoing care |
| Credit | Reduces an issued invoice it names |

**New invoice** (neon1) picks a type. Leaving its lines empty lets 1NEON fill them from the approved option or the receipts. **Save draft** keeps it private. **Issue** numbers it (such as **INV-0039-01**: the proposal's number, or the project key when there's no proposal, and its place in the project), sets its due date (15 days by default), addresses it to the decision maker, or else a client admin, and fixes its contents with a SHA-256 fingerprint. The client is told through the bell and email.

Each invoice opens on its own page, `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{id}`, on neon1's letterhead: from, bill to, the lines, sales tax, the total, credits, payments, the balance due, the terms, and how to pay. It's ready to print or save as a PDF. An invoice reads as **Draft**, **Open**, **Partly paid**, **Overdue** (past its due date with a balance), **Paid in full**, **Void**, or **Credit**.

Paying:

- **Online:** **See and pay**, then **Pay**, opens Stripe Checkout, Stripe's own secure page, for what's left on the invoice. Bank transfer (ACH) comes first, and card is offered too. 1NEON never sees card or bank details. A card payment shows as paid in a moment; a bank payment takes a few business days to clear, and shows once it does. If a bank payment fails, the people who get billing notices are told.
- **By check, Zelle, or wire:** neon1 records it with **Record a payment** when it arrives: the amount, how it arrived, the date, and a check number or confirmation.
- No surcharge is added for any way of paying.

An issued invoice and every payment are permanent. A mistake is fixed with a **credit** that reduces the invoice, or by **voiding** it with a reason (**Void invoice**), and both stay on record. An invoice that has payments can't be voided, so it's credited instead. A copy of every signature, issued invoice, and payment is also kept locked for seven years.

The **Agreements, invoices, and payments** notification group (email on by default) covers the service agreement being signed, invoices issued or voided, and payments that arrive or fail. neon1's drafts never reach the client's bell or email.

## Next step

The top of every project shows **Next step**: the one thing to do now and who it's waiting on. It picks the most pressing of these, in order:

1. For client members, an invoice with a balance: "Invoice INV-0039-01 is ready" (or **overdue**), the amount, and the due date, with **See and pay**.
2. For neon1, invoice drafts: "A deposit invoice is drafted. Check it, then issue.", with **Check invoices**.
3. For neon1, shared options not yet in an issued revision: "Issue the proposal so the client can approve an option" (or its next revision, such as r2), with **Issue the proposal** or **Issue r2**.
4. Options are shared and you may approve: "Choose an option: {n} ready for your approval in Proposal 0039-r1", or that the estimates are due a price check, or that neon1 is preparing the proposal, with **Compare options**.
5. Options are shared and someone else approves: "Waiting on {decision maker} to choose an option", with **See options**.
6. Files are asked for (for client members): "Send {n} files", with **Upload**.
7. You have open items assigned to you: "You have {n} open items here", with **Open**.
8. An option is approved and the project is at or before Decide: "{option} is approved. Next, move the project to {next stage}", with **Move to** for editors.
9. For neon1: "Add options" when none exist yet near Decide, or "Share an option" when options exist but none is shared.
10. Otherwise the stage's goal: "To finish {stage}: {done when}", with **Move to {next stage}** for editors (not past Decide without an approval).
11. "Nothing needs doing right now."

## Health

Health is the team's assessment of how a project is going: **Not assessed**, **On track**, **At risk**, or **Off track**. A new project is Not assessed, and starting work or moving stages never changes it. Editors set it on the Overview, or by posting a status update ("How is it going?"), which also records who assessed it and when.

## Starting a project

**New project** (editors and admins) asks a few short questions: the kind of project (a template), its name, what it is, what will be true when it's done, one real example of how the work happens today, a target date, any sensitive data (PII, PHI, or payment), and optional measures with a baseline and target. Templates start the project with fitting items:

| Template | Key | Starts with |
|---|---|---|
| Blank | PRJ | Nothing |
| Cloud migration | MIG | Discovery questions, servers and files assets, a must-have requirement, cost and downtime measures, a backup restore check, and the handoff checklist |
| Workflow automation | FLOW | Discovery questions, tools and inboxes asset, "nothing is retyped twice", turnaround and staff-time measures, and the handoff checklist |
| AI assistant | AI | Discovery questions, document sources asset, "answers cite their source", time-to-answer and correctness measures, and the handoff checklist |
| Security readiness | SEC | Discovery questions, systems in scope, "MFA on every admin account", an open-findings measure, an access review check, and the handoff checklist |
| Personal or home tech | HOME | "What's not working, in your own words", devices and accounts involved, and "Written steps left behind" |

Every template except Blank and Personal or home tech starts with this handoff checklist:

- Accounts are in the client's name.
- Admin access is transferred to the client.
- Docs are delivered and walked through.
- The people who use it are trained on it.
- Older tools are retired or merged.
- neon1's access is reduced or removed.

## The Overview tab

Overview shows the decision (if any), summary and outcome, measures with progress, the side column (health with who set it and when, stage and dates, the latest update, sensitive-data flags, people, and **Archive this project**), **How is it going?** for posting a status update, and **People on this project** with their roles: lead engineer, sponsor, decision maker, tech contact, stakeholder, and observer. Roles describe what someone does. They never grant access, except that a decision maker may approve.

docs.title: 1NEON guide: every page, what it shows, and who can do what
docs.text:
# 1NEON guide: every page, what it shows, and who can do what

Each signed-in 1NEON page: what it's for, what's on it, its states, and the actions on it with the access each one needs.

Access levels are cumulative. **Viewers** read, comment, add requests, and approve when they're a project's decision maker. **Editors** also add and change work. **Admins** also invite people, change access, change settings, and delete projects, files, and others' comments. Admin actions also need a recent "confirm it's you" (see the people and account guide). neon1, the operator, acts as an admin in every organization but never approves for a client.

## Home

`/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace`. The starting point: what needs you, and what changed lately.

- **Needs you** lists things waiting on you, each with the one action it asks for: **Compare options** (an approval), **Upload file** (a file asked for), or **Open** (your task or item). "You're all caught up" when empty.
- **Coming up** shows this week and the next two as a strip of days, each mark a due date, milestone, or project target, then everything dated in the next six weeks listed by Overdue, This week, Next week, and Later.
- **Get started** is a setup checklist that disappears once done: take the tour; start your first project (editors); invite your team (admins); add a second step for admin actions (admins).
- **Recent activity**: what people did lately, newest first.

## Board

`/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow`. Every project as a card in its stage. Drag a card to move it (editors and admins), or use **Move to** on a phone. Moving forward past Decide without an approved option asks for a reason. Each column shows "Done when" and its project count, and a limit if one is set.

## Projects

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects`. All projects, as a **List** (stage, health, target date; filter by layer; sort by stage, target date, or recent changes) or a **Timeline** (each project drawn from its start to its target date, colored by layer; the dashed line is today, the diamond the target, red stripes time past the target, and each row says its stage and days left). **New project** starts one (editors and admins).

## New project

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new`. A few short steps: pick a template, name it, describe it and its outcome, give one real example, an optional target date, sensitive-data flags, and optional measures. Editors and admins only.

## One project

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}`, with tabs Overview, Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize (`/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, `/normalize`). The header shows the key, the stage and how long it has been there, the name with its health, and the onion. **Next step** sits on top. Details are in the projects guide. Actions:

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| Read, comment on items | Everyone in the organization |
| Add a request | Everyone, viewers too |
| Add, edit, tick off, or delete tasks, questions, measures, checks, and other items | Editors and admins |
| Edit name, summary, outcome, target date; set health; post a status update; move stage; archive | Editors and admins |
| Change people on the project (not the decision maker) | Editors and admins |
| Name or change the decision maker | Admins of the client, after confirming it's them (in N1-0001 also neon1) |
| Approve an option, with a typed signature | The named decision maker; with none named, a client admin. Only from an issued revision, within its price check, once the service agreement is signed |
| Ask neon1 to refresh a revision past its price check | Whoever may approve |
| Initial a purchase neon1 buys; check and accept a handover step | Whoever may approve |
| Add, share, or withdraw options; issue the proposal or its next revision | neon1 only |
| Add a purchase, attach a receipt, mark it bought, installed, or returned | Editors and admins (neon1 marks its own purchases bought only after the decision maker's initials) |
| Read issued invoices; pay one online | Everyone in the client organization |
| Draft, issue, void, or credit an invoice; record a check, Zelle, or wire payment | neon1 only |
| Move to Trash | Admins, after confirming it's them, typing the project's key |

Files asked for show under Needs with **Upload**. The proposal, purchases, invoices, and paying are described in the projects guide. Measures take dated readings. Someone else editing the same item shows as a small avatar beside the project's name.

## The proposal

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal`. The project's proposal on neon1's letterhead: the latest issued revision (such as 0039-r2), or the draft before the first is issued, with earlier revisions marked as replaced. **Print or save as PDF** and **Download Word** keep a copy. Once an option is approved, it shows the signed approval recorded against that revision. Everyone in the organization can read it.

## An invoice

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{id}`. One invoice on neon1's letterhead, ready to print or save as a PDF: its number, dates, bill to, lines, tax, total, credits, payments, the balance due, the terms, and how to pay. **Back to invoices** returns to the project's Invoices. A draft says "Draft, only neon1 sees it. Issuing numbers it and shows it to the client."

## The service agreement

`/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` (signed in) and `/1NEON/agreement` (public). neon1's service agreement, its edition, and its **Signatures**: who signed which edition and when. An admin of the client organization reads it and signs it once, with a typed name and the consent box. On success: "Signed. Thank you; a copy is kept with your organization's records."

## One layer across projects

`/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/{needs|execute|observe|normalize}`. Every project's items for one layer in one list. Open a project to add or change its items.

## People

`/1NEON/o/{org}/people`. Who's in the organization, their title, access, and status.

- **Invite people** (admins): one or more emails, an access level (viewer, editor, or admin), and optional names and titles. Each person gets an email with a link and signs in with a code. Up to 50 at once.
- Each invitation shows whether its email went out: queued, sent, or failed. **Resend** sends it again (rate limited).
- Admins change someone's access or title, or **deactivate** them, which signs them out and ends their access. Reactivating brings them back.
- Member statuses: **Invited** (hasn't signed in yet), **Joined**, **Deactivated**.
- neon1's own access shows without a way to change it.

## Files

`/1NEON/o/{org}/documents`. Every file shared in the organization. **Upload** (everyone in the organization, viewers too) a file up to 100 MB, and pick its project, or none for a general file. Each file goes through states: **Receiving** (uploading), **Checking** (virus scan and size check), **Ready** (clean, opens or downloads), **Rejected** (the scan found a threat), or **Failed** (missing, the wrong size, or a scan that couldn't finish). PDFs, pictures, and text open in a new tab; anything else downloads. The uploader and admins can delete a file. No passwords, keys, or regulated data without an agreement that covers it.

## Insights

`/1NEON/o/{org}/insights`. Charts from the organization's own data: open and overdue work, the on-time rate, days to a decision, measures at target, items finished per week for the last eight weeks, projects by layer, and health. Work counts as finished on the day it was marked done. The page explains how each number is counted.

## Settings

`/1NEON/o/{org}/settings`. Who signed the service agreement and which edition, or "not signed yet", with **Read and sign** (or **Read it** once signed). Then the stages on the board. Each row: name, layer, "Done when", and an optional limit; **Show** or **Hide**; reorder. **Save workflow** saves all at once (admins, after confirming it's them). A stage that holds projects can't be removed.

## Your profile

`/1NEON/me`. Name, title, phone (only you see it), theme (Awake, Matrix, or Device), menu (Default or Mini), and **Notifications**: for each group (files; people and access; decisions and options; agreements, invoices, and payments; workflow and stages; comments; updates and items; sign-ins) whether it reaches you by email, by text, or neither. Then **Save**. Also here: texts (add a mobile number, agree to texts, confirm the code), **Two-step verification** at `#security` (passkey, authenticator app, text-message codes), **Replay the tutorial**, and **Sign out**. Two-step changes and signing out take effect at once.

## All clients

`/1NEON/all/workflow`, neon1 only. Every client's projects on one read-only board, **By organization** (each organization with its client ID, such as N1-0001, and how many projects are active) or **One board**. To change anything, open the client.

## Public pages

The sign-in screen (`/1NEON/`), FAQs, the service agreement, the sample project, the guided walkthrough, the interactive demo, and the policies need no account. Neo on the sign-in screen is the public Neo, which only knows neon1's public pages.

docs.title: 1NEON guide: sign-in, confirming it's you, notifications, and texts
docs.text:
# 1NEON guide: sign-in, confirming it's you, notifications, and texts

How people get into 1NEON, why admin actions ask to confirm it's you, the three second steps, notifications, texts, and what to do when something is lost.

## Getting in

1NEON is invitation only. An admin of the organization, or neon1, invites a person by email. The person opens the link, enters their email, and signs in with a code sent to that email (8 digits, valid for a few minutes, in the browser that asked for it), or with a passkey once they've added one. There are no passwords. If a code doesn't arrive, check spam or promotions, wait a minute, then **Send a new code**. The first sign-in offers a one-minute welcome tour, with **Remind me next time** and **Skip**. It can be replayed from **?** or the profile.

Your email address is how 1NEON knows you, and it can't be changed on the profile. A new address means an admin invites the new one and deactivates the old one.

## Confirming it's you

Admin actions need a recent confirmation with a second step, so a stolen email account isn't enough to make changes. They are: inviting people, changing access or deactivating someone, changing settings (stages), naming a decision maker, deleting a project, and deleting someone else's comment or file. When needed, 1NEON asks "Confirm it's you" and offers the person's second steps. Once confirmed, it isn't asked again for 12 hours in that sign-in.

The three second steps, added on the profile under **Two-step verification** (`/1NEON/me#security`):

- **Passkey**: face, fingerprint, or device PIN. Fastest and phishing-resistant. Once added, sign-in offers it first.
- **Authenticator app**: **Set up**, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type its 6-digit code.
- **Text-message codes**: once a mobile number is verified for texts.

A second one is a backup. Lost one: confirm with another, remove the lost one, and add a new one. Lost all of them: email hello@neon1.tech from the account's address. There's no self-service reset, and email alone isn't enough, since a stolen mailbox is what the second step guards against. neon1 first confirms who it is by calling a phone number already on record for the person or their organization (never one given in the email), plus the written OK of another admin when the organization has one. Then the lost methods are removed, the removal is noted with its date, and the person is emailed; they add a new one on their profile. Email codes still sign you in meanwhile. The second step is only for admin actions.

## Notifications

The bell glows when something new happens, and opening it lists what changed and marks it seen. Important changes also email you. Each person chooses per group on the profile:

| Group | What counts | Email by default |
|---|---|---|
| Files | A file is uploaded or removed | Yes |
| People and access | Someone is invited, joins, or changes access | Yes |
| Decisions and options | An option is proposed or approved | Yes |
| Workflow and stages | A project is created, moves stage, or goes to Trash, or the stages change | Yes |
| Comments | Someone comments on an item | No |
| Updates and items | Status updates, requests, tasks, measures, and other items | No |
| Sign-ins | Someone in the organization signs in | No |

## Texts

Once texts are switched on for the portal, a person adds a mobile number on the profile, agrees to texts, saves, then types the 6-digit code 1NEON texts them. Texts only say something new is waiting, with a link. They never name the organization, projects, or files. Reply STOP to any text to turn them off, and agreeing again turns them back on. Changing the number turns texts and text codes off until the new number is confirmed.

## Your data, billing, and urgent problems

Invoices and payments are in each project's Execute layer, under Invoices (see the projects guide). There's no export button, so ask hello@neon1.tech for a copy of the organization's data. Data is kept as the record of the work unless the organization asks for deletion. neon1 is one person working planned hours, with no 24/7 response. For an emergency, contact the provider responsible first. Report a security problem in the portal to security@neon1.tech.
